title: Mr. Wonderful Warns Most AI Data Centers Will Shut Down (Here’s Who Wins)
creator: MarketBeat
summary: MarketBeat interviews Kevin O'Leary ('Mr. Wonderful') on the AI data-center build-out. O'Leary frames investing around two verticals for the next five years: power, and AI compute plus cloud storage, arguing demand for compute is roughly 3x current capacity and insatiable into Q4 2027, so he sees no slowdown despite this week's volatility. His central warning is that 60-65% of announced data-center projects will be shut down or never built in the next 24 months, due to fatal flaws in water, fiber or power, or political moratoria — making permitted sites with a path to power, permit and profitability scarce and valuable. A 1.4GW project costs about $16bn ($8bn equity / $8bn debt), with $20-30m per GW in pre-planning alone. He discloses holding Bitzero (ticker AIBZ, captioned 'Bit Zero'), a public Norway/Finland hydro/nuclear-powered developer he invested in pre-IPO and likes for liquidity, alongside private projects in Utah and Alberta; data centers are over 20% of his book. He also names Microsoft as a lower-volatility behemoth AI name investors can buy. No explicit buy recommendation is made for any ticker — AIBZ is a disclosed, bullish holding and MSFT a passing example, both tracked as UNCERTAIN. Captions garble names occasionally ('Olirri' for O'Leary, 'bid zero' for Bitzero).
